card.name: Words before a treatment target or object
card.fires_on: Short linking or ending pieces in clinical prose, such as "of" after "effectiveness", "to" after "best", or the end of words like muscle relaxant and antidote. It marks a spot where a specific noun phrase about a treatment or drug is expected next.

modes.label: Of after effectiveness
modes.description: The word "of" right after "effectiveness", before the treatment being judged.
modes.example: Patients were dosed in a range of 10 to 60 mg/day in the clinical trials demonstrating the effectiveness<< of>> paroxetine tablets.

modes.label: Ends of drug-class words
modes.description: The last piece of a drug-class or treatment word, or a modifier before a drug class.
modes.example: decrease the dosage of tapentadol hydrochloride oral solution and/or the muscle relax<<ant>> as necessary.

modes.label: Other linking words in treatment phrases
modes.description: Words such as "to", "approach" or "directed" in phrases about how a treatment is applied.
modes.example: Tests were done to see how best<< to>> apply it.

card.plain: It fires on small words and word endings just before the text names a treatment, drug or inhibitor.
